leads.name: The Plane of Agia Paraskevi, Tsagarada (Pelion)
leads.why: Tipped by Hidde 2026-08-14 from a newsletter he received (sender never published, per the standing rule). The claims to verify, none verified yet: scientists estimate over 1,000 years, which would make it one of Europe's oldest trees; trunk circumference around 14m; one heavy limb rests on a pillar; it IS the village square of Tsagarada (church, playground, cafes and festivals all under it), so access is public by its nature. One CC BY-SA 4.0 photo on Commons (File:Tsagarada Plane Tree.jpg), no geotag; coordinates deliberately not guessed. WHERE IT CAN SHIP: no city can host it (Tsagarada is a village on Pelion, over an hour from Volos, beyond the 30-minute day-trip rule), so its home is The Great Planes of Europe or an oldest-trees collection, which today requires a Contract D schema change (free entries not tied to a city page) and therefore Hidde's yes. CLAUDE.md already anticipates exactly this: 'a two-street village with one fine oak is a collection entry, not a city'.
